literal.prompt: Какой действующий вулкан расположен на острове Росса в Антарктиде?

literalGroups.primaryGround: The prompt’s target is an active volcano at Ross Island in Antarctica: GVP identifies Erebus as the southernmost active volcano in Antarctica and locates it on Ross Island (L80,L116); retained BAS also labels Mount Erebus as Ross Island (L43@P1). GVP profiles ground the alternatives: Etna in Italy’s Sicily Volcanic Province with recent confirmed activity (Italy page L56-L63,L75); Fuji is a volcano on Honshu (Fujisan page L105); Kilimanjaro is a volcanic massif of three edifices in Tanzania (Kilimanjaro page L318-L320). Only Erebus fits the requested place.
literalGroups.locator: GVP Erebus L80,L116-L117; BAS L43@P1; GVP Italy L56-L63,L75; Fujisan L105; Kilimanjaro L318-L320.

literalGroups.primaryGround: GVP reports the active lava lake in Erebus’s summit crater since at least 1972 (L80,L116-L117,L667-L668), supporting the explanation’s crater/lava-lake claim.
literalGroups.locator: GVP Erebus L80,L116-L117; the persistent lava lake is also described at L667-L668.
